root_cause: The ARM64 cross-compilation build uses a precompiled header (cmake_pch.hxx.gch) for the openvino_shape_inference target that was generated by a different/incompatible toolchain state (e.g. produced by a prior compiler invocation, sccache-restored artifact, or a container/cache reused across an incompatible GCC configuration for aarch64-linux-gnu-g++). GCC's PCH validation rejects the .gch file as 'not a PCH file', and because the build treats warnings as errors (-Werror -Winvalid-pch), this becomes a hard failure rather than a silent PCH-miss-and-recompile. The failure is isolated to the core shape_inference target and is unrelated to the PR's NPU plugin changes (ze_graph_ext_wrappers.cpp/dynamic_graph.cpp) — none of the failing translation units are among the PR's changed files, confirming this is an infrastructure/caching artifact rather than a code defect introduced by PR #37942.
reproduction_steps: N/A (depends on a stale build/sccache/PCH artifact reused between CI runs on the aks-lin-x64-build-16c32gb runner; not reliably reproducible outside the affected CI container/cache state). Locally, one can approximate it by manually corrupting or reusing a cmake_pch.hxx.gch from an incompatible compiler/flags combination and rebuilding the same target with -Werror -Winvalid-pch.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Build / Build' job (or the whole run) — a clean CMake/ninja build regenerates cmake_pch.hxx.gch from scratch and should clear a stale/corrupted PCH artifact.
If the failure recurs across multiple runs, invalidate/clear the sccache and any ccache/build-dir caches used by the ARM64 cross-compilation job to remove the incompatible cached PCH.

Consider whether the PCH generation step ties its cache key to the exact compiler + flags (e.g. -std=c++17, -fPIC visibility flags) used for openvino_shape_inference, so a partial cache restore cannot mix an incompatible .gch with the current invocation.
No code change is required in PR #37942; the NPU-only diff does not touch src/core/shape_inference.
prevention_strategies: Ensure PCH artifacts are keyed/invalidated together with the exact compiler version, target flags, and toolchain (host vs. aarch64-linux-gnu cross-compiler) so a partially-restored or cross-job cache cannot supply an incompatible .gch file. Consider adding a build step that removes stale *.gch files before a fresh CMake configure when the compiler or flags used to produce them may have changed, or disable -Werror=invalid-pch failure escalation in favor of an automatic PCH regeneration.
historical_context: No prior CI Doctor MQ investigation or pattern record for this cmake_pch invalid-PCH signature was found in the merge-queue knowledge base; this is the first recorded occurrence (pattern count = 1).
